title: [CS-01] Capture and review the viewed product
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to review a product captured from the active page so I save the intended item.

Implemented: user-initiated extraction; editable name, price, retailer, identifiers, variant and condition; captured image or placeholder; manual fallback; scoped activeTab access. Fixture and DOM tests are recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md. The actual Alpha ZIP, toolbar activeTab grant and fixture capture passed in real Chrome under REL-01. Current live retailer markup remains the CS-11 field gate.

title: [CS-02] Universal saved cart and budget
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want saved products from different stores in one cart so I can plan a purchase.

Implemented: local persistence; quantity and notes editing; removal; save-for-later; budget and item subtotal; consistent retailer links. Comparison shows shipping and tax separately. Behavioral and DOM validation is recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-03] Transparent matched-offer comparison
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to compare offers for the same model and variant so I can choose deliberately.

Implemented: observed/manual offers; identity, variant and condition checks; item, shipping, tax, membership, discount and cashback breakdown; unknown required costs remain unknown; quantity-aware totals; ranking by total, delivery, returns or pickup with preference eligibility. Examples are labeled. Automated cross-store discovery remains CS-12; current real prices require user capture or entry.

title: [CS-04] Observed price history
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want a record of observed prices so I can see changes over time.

Implemented: captures and offer edits store timestamped price observations with their source; comparison displays the saved retailer's observed range. Latest availability remains on each offer. These are user observations, not a complete market price history. Validation: docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-05] Watched price-drop and restock alerts
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want watched changes surfaced when I capture an item again so I can act on new information.

Implemented: opted-in price targets and restock watches; transition detection on new captures or offer edits; in-app notifications; optional Chrome desktop notification permission. Core, storage and DOM tests cover observed transitions. Native OS notification delivery remains platform field scope under CS-19; unattended polling remains CS-14.

title: [CS-06] Manual order records and tracking links
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to record orders so I can keep delivery notes together.

Implemented: manual create, edit and delete; product, retailer, quantity, order status, order/expected dates, notes, tracking number and safe tracking URL. Invalid quantities and impossible dates are rejected. A separate carrier-name field and live carrier feed are not implemented; source-backed updates remain CS-15. Validation: docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-07] Full-obligation installment calculator
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to estimate installment costs so I understand entered financing terms.

Implemented: purchase amount, payment count, entered interest amount and fees, first payment date and day interval; exact-cent schedule and total owed; stated late fee shown separately. Zero amounts are valid. No provider offer, APR calculation or loan eligibility decision is implied. Validation: docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-08] Local data controls
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want control of my data so I can back it up or remove it.

Implemented: JSON export/import, schema and ID validation, atomic rejection of malformed imports, preserved links/observations, historical alert messages not replayed, notifications disabled after import, and confirmed deletion. Sample backups cannot enter the real workspace. Storage and DOM checks are recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md; actual Chrome backup export/import and browser downloads passed under REL-01.

title: [CS-09] Isolated illustrative sample workspace
label: alpha
body:
As a first-time tester, I want optional sample data so I can try the flows safely.

Implemented: empty real first run; separate labeled sample workspace with products, offers, history, alerts and orders; reset and exit controls; backup provenance preserved. Samples cannot be imported into the real workspace, even after their offers are removed. Validation: docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-10] Alpha installation documentation and feedback routes
label: alpha
body:
As a reference user, I want install instructions and a feedback route so I can test the alpha.

Prepared: README, release notes, deterministic runtime ZIP/checksum, GitHub issue forms accepting task outcomes, times, ratings and written feedback, private reply protocol, draft invitation and unassigned R01-R10 roster. Publication is REL-02/03/08. Recruitment, actual sending and collected feedback remain REL-04/05/06; documents and empty participant slots do not establish those outcomes.

title: [CS-21] Static browser demo
label: alpha
body:
As a reviewer, I want a browser demo so I can explore CartScope without installing it.

Implemented: the same static interface and production state consumer using browser localStorage; labeled sample mode and manual entry; extension-only capture/desktop notifications clearly explained; no AWS setup. Local demo build and DOM flows are recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md. Public GitHub Pages hosting and real Chrome navigation/persistence checks passed under REL-08.

title: [CS-11] Validate capture on reference users’ stores
label: next-sprint
body:
As a shopper, I want reliable capture on the stores I use so I make fewer manual corrections.

Sprint: Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. Priority: P1. Proposed owners: Kartik (engineering), Jake (acceptance). Acceptance: select current stores from consenting testers; retain permitted page examples and add fixtures where needed; exercise user-initiated toolbar capture and editable review; record attempted captures, corrected fields, failures and actual denominators with browser/OS/version; reproduce and link defects. Deterministic historical fixtures do not close live-store field validation. Dates and owners are confirmed at planning.

title: [CS-12] Authorized automatic cross-store offer discovery
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want matched retailer offers found automatically so I need less manual entry.

Priority: P1. Proposed owners: Kartik (integration), Jake (scope). Acceptance: select an authorized feed/source; document access and refresh limits; normalize canonical identifiers, model, variant and condition; reject mismatches; distinguish live/stale observations and missing shipping/tax. Use the simplest permitted integration; AWS is not a prerequisite. Confirm sprint dates and owners at planning.

November 14 planning update: deferred behind Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. This source-dependent integration is not implemented or committed to the fielding sprint.

title: [CS-13] Resolve observed Alpha usability blockers
label: next-sprint
body:
As a reference tester, I want reported blockers fixed so the save-and-compare flow is usable.

Sprint: Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. Priority: P1. Proposed owners: Jake (triage), Kartik (fixes). Acceptance: use real support/feedback reports; reproduce selected blockers; assign severity and owner; add a meaningful regression check; record version and resolution; verify the changed task with affected testers where possible. Keep installed-extension and browser-demo results separate. No reproduced incident, response time or user acceptance is claimed yet. Depends on actual reports under REL-06 and CS-23.

title: [CS-14] Opt-in unattended price checks
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want watched prices checked while I am away so I can hear about meaningful changes.

Priority: P2; conditional on an authorized source from CS-12. Acceptance: explicit opt-in, supported refresh policy, notification frequency controls and deduplication, source timestamps and availability evidence, and justified permissions/privacy handling. Current Alpha evaluates only user-triggered observations. Confirm feasibility before committing the sprint.

November 14 planning update: deferred behind Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. This source-dependent integration is not implemented or committed to the fielding sprint.

title: [CS-15] Authorized order updates
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want order updates imported from a supported source so I can stop editing statuses manually.

Priority: P2; conditional on permitted carrier/retailer source access. Acceptance: choose an authorized integration; protect order credentials; normalize status mapping; show last-sync time; preserve manual correction and fallback. Current Alpha has manually entered order records. Confirm feasibility before committing the sprint.

November 14 planning update: deferred behind Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. This source-dependent integration is not implemented or committed to the fielding sprint.

title: [CS-16] Optional account and cross-device cart synchronization
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want an optional account to synchronize my saved cart across devices.

Entry criteria: demand demonstrated by feedback, agreed identity/storage architecture and deletion policy, explicit opt-in. No account or cloud service is required for the current Alpha.

title: [CS-17] Optional hosted price and availability refresh service
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want authorized offer refreshes that can continue independently of my browser.

Entry criteria: an actual need after Alpha; authorized source selected; agreed cost, freshness, monitoring, retention and security requirements; no retailer secrets in the extension. No hosted service or AWS deployment is required for the current demo.

title: [CS-18] Provider-backed BNPL comparison
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want current provider-backed payment terms so I can compare full obligations.

Entry criteria: current terms and integration permission obtained; jurisdiction/disclosure requirements reviewed; no estimated APR or invented financing offer. The Alpha calculator accepts user-entered terms only.

title: [CS-19] Accessibility and browser support expansion
label: next-sprint
body:
As a shopper, I want the documented Chrome installation and core flows checked on the platforms our testers use.

Sprint: Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. Priority: P1. Proposed owner: Kartik, with consenting reference testers. Acceptance: define supported Chrome/OS combinations; manually test installation/update/uninstall, keyboard focus and principal tasks; test opted-in native notifications on an actual OS; record environment, attempted checks, results and limitations; triage accessibility/support defects. Historical DOM checks and automated Ubuntu Chrome checks do not establish screen-reader behavior, every OS, or current live-store compatibility. Broader browser coverage remains future scope.

title: [CS-20] Chrome Web Store beta distribution
label: next-sprint
body:
As a shopper, I want a Chrome Web Store listing so installation and updates are easier.

Sprint: Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. Priority: P1. Planned distribution work, not published: no verified Store URL, publisher access or approval is recorded. Acceptance: current listing/privacy/permission/reviewer materials and assets ready; verified launch candidate ZIP and test evidence; authorized publisher uploads the candidate and records the submission confirmation under REL-12; close only when a public approved listing resolves with the expected identity/version under REL-13. GitHub Alpha publication and a prepared listing kit do not close this story.

Proposed owners: Eashan and Jake, with Kartik supplying release links.

Collect task completion/time and ease, clarity, usefulness and confidence ratings plus confusing/missing information and requested improvements. Distinguish installed-extension and browser-demo results; report actual denominators. Feed reproduced blockers into CS-13. Close only after real responses and a readout exist; targets are not results.

If the team supplies its existing board, verify access and reconcile stories, status and next-sprint priorities with this GitHub tracker. GitHub Issues and docs/SPRINT_BOARD.md satisfy the current assignment's similar-issue-tracker option. title: [EP-01] Screenshot capture and review
label: backlog
body:
Planned epic. Feature: screenshot-assisted product entry. Child implementation story: CS-24. Planning source: the owner's October 22 chat feedback requested screenshot capture, price guidance and occasion folders. This is feature input, not evidence of completed implementation, interviews or a ten-user study.

The shipped Alpha reads product-page markup or accepts manual entry; it does not extract product details from screenshots. Epic completion requires an implemented capture/import path, explicit review, privacy/permission decisions and verified user-task results.

title: [CS-24] Save a product from a user-supplied screenshot
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want to capture product details from a screenshot so I can save an item when page extraction is unavailable.

Parent: EP-01. Feature: screenshot-assisted capture. Not implemented. Acceptance: agree on a user-selected image or explicit visible-tab capture path; document processing location and any added permissions; propose detected product fields with uncertainty; require editable review before saving; preserve screenshot/source provenance without treating image content as instructions; provide manual fallback; test unsupported, ambiguous and sensitive-content cases. No OCR provider or screenshot retention policy has been selected. Scope decisions are CS-27; implementation follows approved acceptance.

title: [EP-02] Evidence-based price guidance
label: backlog
body:
Planned epic. Feature: price guidance from observed evidence. Child implementation story: CS-25. Planning source: the owner's October 22 chat feedback requested screenshot capture, price guidance and occasion folders. This is feature input, not evidence of completed implementation, interviews or a ten-user study.

The shipped Alpha shows recorded observations and compares entered offers; it does not provide buy/wait recommendations, a fair-market valuation or price forecasts. Epic completion requires defined guidance rules, source coverage and freshness, uncertainty states and behavioral validation.

title: [CS-25] Explain price guidance using recorded observations
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want price guidance with its evidence so I can decide whether an observed offer suits my purchase.

Parent: EP-02. Feature: price guidance. Not implemented. Acceptance: define the guidance rule and minimum observation coverage; show source, timestamps, comparable model/variant/condition and sample size; distinguish item price from complete cost; show insufficient-data or stale-data states; explain recommendations in plain language; keep labeled samples separate; test sparse, stale, mismatched and conflicting observations. Do not invent a market-wide feed or present a future price as known. Scope decisions are CS-27.

title: [EP-03] Organize shopping by occasion
label: backlog
body:
Planned epic. Feature: occasion folders. Child implementation story: CS-26. Planning source: the owner's October 22 chat feedback requested screenshot capture, price guidance and occasion folders. This is feature input, not evidence of completed implementation, interviews or a ten-user study.

The shipped Alpha has one cart and save-for-later; it has no occasion folders. Epic completion requires a defined collection model, usable folder actions and verified persistence/backup behavior.

title: [CS-26] Group saved products into occasion folders
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want folders for an occasion so I can organize related purchases without losing saved items.

Parent: EP-03. Feature: occasion folders. Not implemented. Acceptance: create, rename and delete a folder; add/remove saved products; define whether an item can belong to several folders and how folder budgets work; keep products when a folder is deleted unless the user separately removes them; persist membership; migrate existing carts; preserve relationships through validated export/import and sample isolation; test empty, renamed and deleted folders. Scope decisions are CS-27.

title: [CS-23] Run field validation and support intake
label: next-sprint
body:
As a reference user, I want a clear support route so installation and shopping problems can be investigated.

Sprint: Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. Priority: P1. Proposed owners: Jake (triage), Eashan (reference-user coordination), Kartik (technical support). Acceptance: publish a working support/bug route and known-issues guidance; identify the exact candidate or Store version; collect consenting testers' environments, task outcomes, timing and written reports; record actual acknowledgement, reproduction and resolution dates; link defects to CS-13; provide install/update/uninstall and backup recovery guidance. Define response targets at team planning; targets are not measured service results. Recruitment and sending remain REL-04/05/14.

title: [CS-27] Define acceptance for requested screenshot, guidance and folder features
label: next-sprint
body:
As the product team, we want agreed acceptance for the requested features so later implementation addresses the owner's actual workflows.

Sprint: Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. Priority: P2 after launch/field blockers. Proposed owners: Jake (scope), Eashan (workflow review), Kartik (feasibility). Acceptance: review the October 22 chat requests; clarify one concrete task per feature; define screenshot processing/retention and permission choices, price-guidance evidence and unknown states, and folder membership/budget/deletion rules; estimate and prioritize EP-01/02/03 with CS-24/25/26; record agreed acceptance and unresolved questions. This is planning/discovery only; it cannot mark those features implemented.

title: [REL-12] Submit the candidate for Chrome Web Store review
label: release
body: Sprint: Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. Depends on verified candidate evidence and an authorized Store publisher session. Acceptance: confirm product identity CartScope — Shopping desk and candidate version 0.1.2; complete listing, privacy, permissions, assets and reviewer instructions; upload the verified runtime ZIP; submit through the authorized publisher dashboard; record actual item ID, submitted version, submission time and review status. A prepared kit or uploaded draft is not a submitted or approved extension. No Store submission evidence is currently recorded.

title: [REL-13] Verify the approved public Chrome Web Store listing
label: release
body: Sprint: Sprint 2.E Fielding & Support. Depends on REL-12 and external Store review. Acceptance: open the actual public listing and verify title, item ID, publisher, available version and install route; record its real URL, approval/publication status and check time; verify installation/update from the Store on a supported environment; replace pending Store references only after verification. Acceptance: confirm ten consenting reference recipients under REL-04; personalize/send the reference-user announcement through an authorized account; publish approved public copy to selected authorized channels; include the verified install/release links, support route, quantitative task outcomes/times/ratings, qualitative comments route and an invitation to leave a voluntary honest Chrome Web Store review after use. Record actual send/publication dates and channel evidence privately where it contains personal information. Do not claim messages, reviews or user outcomes that have not occurred.
